parts: Please review the manuscript in shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/mixed_character_families/, and the continuation note in notes/23_SIGNED_BILINEAR_CONTINUATION_20261009.md, and follow with the appropriate next steps
I’ll review the manuscript and continuation note, check the mathematical gap they identify, and carry out the next steps supported by that review.

The short-cofactor removal checks out so far, including its cross terms. The remaining moment is still open. I’m working on an exact dyadic formulation that retains the unbalanced factors and short quotients, while the parallel audits check the manuscript and the available transform estimates.

The review has yielded a larger controlled sector: the same source inputs allow the cutoff to grow from \(U^{1/10}\) to \(U^{r/2-1/4}\), with the same guaranteed saving for all cross terms. I’ll add that proof, the dyadic cover, and the exact prime-extraction rules to the manuscript and a new continuation note. The remaining \(1/700\) moment still needs an analytic estimate.

The new proofs are integrated, and the manuscript compiles successfully. The smooth transform also admits bounds for the first zero term and the residual unit exception at the second zero frequency. The new checker passed 33,662 exact assertions; I’m finishing the review record and indexes. These results narrow the work, but the nonzero-frequency estimate remains open.

Reviewed and updated the [manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/mixed_character_families/mixed_character_reductions.tex).

The [new continuation note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/mixed_character_families/notes/24_ADAPTIVE_COFACTOR_AND_DYADIC_KERNEL_20261009.md) establishes:

- A larger conditional cofactor cutoff, \(U^{r/2-1/4}\), retaining the same complete cross-term saving.
- The exact dyadic partition and prime-extraction identities, including unbalanced factors, short quotients and physical zeros.
- Conditional bounds for both smooth zero-frequency contributions.

I also corrected frequency-scale notation and clarified historical targets. The manuscript compiled successfully, and **33,662 new exact finite assertions passed**.

The remaining nonzero-frequency estimate with saving \(1/700\) is still unproved. The [review record](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/reviews/MIXED_ADAPTIVE_DYADIC_REVIEW_20261009.md) documents the assumptions, verification and precise next proof obligation.
Excellent, please continue with the next estimate
I’ll work on the remaining nonzero-frequency estimate, testing the exact marked coefficients against the available bounds and looking for a provable gain.

There are two promising findings. The large common factor shared by the two truncated inverse factors appears removable with all cross terms controlled. Separately, a test of the unrestricted smooth enlargement exposes a principal-row obstruction. I’m checking both proofs; the distinction matters because the original selected-family target may remain viable while that stronger enlargement fails.

The common-factor removal checks out: its response square saves \(1/125\), and its complete interaction with the remaining inverse saves at least \(79927/20000000\).

The broader smooth test also fails in a precisely specified principal-compatible class. I’ll record that obstruction with its scope and update the next estimate to retain the selected row restrictions or use a separately justified centered comparison.

The new estimate controls the large common factor of the two inverse factors, including all cross terms. The full selected moment remains open. I’m finishing the audit record, including the obstruction to the broader smooth estimate and its precise scope.

The audits passed, and the updated manuscript compiles. The combined removals retain a saving of \(7979/2000000\), which exceeds the required \(1/700\). The remaining estimate concerns the selected rows with a small inverse-factor common part; the unrestricted uncentered smooth replacement fails in the principal-compatible class examined here.

Continued in [Note 25](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/mixed_character_families/notes/25_SQUAREPART_REMOVAL_AND_SMOOTH_OBSTRUCTION_20261009.md) and incorporated the results into the manuscript.

- Proved, under the existing inputs, large common-factor removal with square saving \(1/125\) and complete cross-term saving at least \(79927/20000000\).
- Proved that the unrestricted uncentered smooth target fails in a principal-compatible class.

The original selected \(1/700\) target remains open. The next estimate must control the surviving small common-factor correlation while retaining the selected row restrictions.

The manuscript compiles; **725,761 exact finite checks passed**. Assumptions, proof scope and verification are recorded in the [review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/quasi-rh-exponent-descent/reviews/MIXED_SQUAREPART_AND_SMOOTH_REVIEW_20261009.md).
